newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban said to give gas project go-ahead.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban said to give gas project go-ahead.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban militia leaders held talks with Pakistani officials on Sunday and gave the go-ahead for a gas pipeline and rail link between Pakistan and Central Asia, Taleban sources said.

The sources told the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press that the agreement was reached in talks that took place in the southern Afghan city of Kandahar between the Taleban's supreme leader Mullah Mohammed Omar and Najmuddin Sheikh, the top civil servant at the Pakistani Foreign Ministry.

The sources, contacted by telephone in Kandahar, said Mullah Mohammed Hassan, deputy leader of the interim ruling shura (council) in Kabul, as well as the governor of Kandahar and other Taleban leaders took part in the talks.
The agreement stipulated that Afghans would supply labour for the projects, Afghan cities on the pipeline route would receive gas and the Afghan government would get transit fees.
The sources said an Argentine company would carry out the gas pipeline project. No immediate confirmation was available.
Bridas of Argentina and Unocal of the United States have both shown interest in the past in building a gas pipeline from Turkmenistan to Pakistan across Afghanistan.
Unocal also wants to build an oil pipeline from Turkmenistan to a terminal on Pakistan's southern coast.

The Taleban and the Pakistanis also discussed a road link to Central Asia and a project to improve the road between Spin Boldak on the Pakistan border and Kabul via Kandahar, but did not reach a final agreement, the Taleban sources said.
Pakistani officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
